pharm: Systemic alkalinising agent (citrate salt); raises urinary pH
quick: 4 g dissolved in water three times daily after meals
Take after meals, well diluted in water
Use only if clearly necessary; caution (sodium load)

summary: Disodium hydrogen citrate is an oral urinary alkalinising agent used to relieve the discomfort of mild urinary-tract infection and cystitis and to raise urinary pH, for example in the prevention of uric acid stones and during certain drug therapies. It works as a systemic alkaliniser after metabolism of citrate to bicarbonate. Because it supplies sodium, caution is needed in renal impairment, cardiac disease, and hypertension.
indications: Symptomatic relief of discomfort in mild urinary-tract infection / cystitis
Alkalinisation of urine (e.g. uric acid stone prevention)
Adjunctive urinary alkalinisation during certain drug therapies

dosage.c: Relief of mild cystitis / UTI discomfort (adult)
dosage.d: 4 g dissolved in water three times daily after meals
dosage.n: Short-term symptomatic use; seek review if symptoms persist beyond a few days

dosage.d: Dose adjusted to achieve target urinary pH

admin: Dissolve the dose fully in a glass of water before taking
Take after meals to reduce gastric irritation
Maintain a good fluid intake during treatment
Use short term for symptomatic cystitis relief unless directed otherwise
Monitor urinary pH when used for sustained alkalinisation
moa: After absorption, citrate is metabolised to bicarbonate, producing a systemic alkalinising effect that increases the renal excretion of bicarbonate and raises urinary pH. Alkaline urine reduces the burning discomfort of cystitis and increases the solubility of uric acid, helping to prevent uric acid crystal and stone formation.

absolute: Hyperkalaemia or conditions requiring strict sodium restriction with combined salts
monitor: Serum sodium and potassium (if combined salts)

preg: Use only if clearly necessary; the sodium content warrants caution in pregnancy, particularly with hypertension, oedema, or cardiac disease.
lact: Generally considered compatible with breastfeeding when used short term, but use with caution and only when needed.
renal: Use with caution; avoid in significant or severe renal impairment because of the risk of sodium overload and electrolyte/acid-base disturbance.
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment required for hepatic impairment.

major: Potassium-sparing diuretics or potassium supplements - hyperkalaemia risk if combined with potassium citrate salts
moderate: Drugs whose renal excretion is pH-dependent - alkaline urine increases excretion of acidic drugs (e.g. salicylates) and decreases excretion of basic drugs (e.g. quinidine, amphetamines)
minor: Methenamine (hexamine) - alkaline urine reduces its antibacterial efficacy
interactions.food: Take after meals, dissolved in water, to minimise gastric irritation
interactions.diagnostics: Raises urinary pH; may affect urine tests and pH-dependent assays

serious: Sodium overload (oedema, worsening hypertension or heart failure)
Hyperkalaemia if combined with potassium salts
emergency: Severe fluid overload / pulmonary oedema in cardiac or renal patients

monitoring: Serum electrolytes (sodium, and potassium if combined salts)
Blood pressure and signs of fluid retention
counsel: Always dissolve the dose fully in water before drinking
Take after meals and drink plenty of fluids
This eases the burning discomfort but is not an antibiotic; see your doctor if symptoms last more than a couple of days or worsen
Tell your clinician if you have heart problems, high blood pressure, or kidney disease
Report swelling of ankles, breathlessness, or significant weight gain
pk: Urinary alkalinisation within a few hours
Several hours; supports divided daily dosing
Store in a dry place below 25-30°C; keep granules/sachets sealed
pearls: Not FDA-approved; record based on EMA/SmPC/BNF sources; pending clinical review.
Provides symptomatic relief for mild cystitis by alkalinising the urine; it is not an antibacterial treatment
Significant sodium load - use cautiously in cardiac failure, hypertension, and renal impairment
Avoid concurrent methenamine, which requires acidic urine to work
Alkaline urine alters excretion of pH-dependent drugs; review co-medications
Monitor urinary pH when used for sustained alkalinisation such as uric acid stone prevention
missed: If a dose is missed, take it when remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose, in which case skip it and resume the normal schedule. Do not take a double dose.
overdose: Excessive intake can cause metabolic alkalosis, hypernatraemia, fluid overload, and (with combined potassium salts) hyperkalaemia. Stop the drug and manage supportively with electrolyte and acid-base correction and monitoring; severe alkalosis or fluid overload may require specific medical or renal support. Maintain adequate hydration and monitor cardiac and renal status.
